label: late original/delimiter steps of long sequences starting "c k"
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.006% of steps). It fires only at t = 5..9, on the last one or two original tokens or on the <DEL> step of long sequences (L = 7..9). It never fires in the copy phase. Activation is driven mainly by the sequence opening: first_tok c gives 17x lift and 64% of mass, w and k are weaker, and the strongest examples begin "c k". The input token f (12x lift) and <DEL> are typical firing inputs. Even with these conditions most matching steps stay silent (precision about 0.2), so the feature looks like a sparse conjunction on top of an opening-token signal. The best predicate (late step, opening c k) gets F1 of about 0.25 and mass recall of about 0.43. Widening it to openings c/k/w raises mass recall to 0.83, but precision falls below 1%. Not checked: what controls magnitude beyond the c-k opening and late position.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+4.70), orig1=k (+4.70), orig2=k (+3.30), prev_tok=0 (+2.97), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=f (+2.72), phase=0 & in_tok=f (+2.72). Lower it: next_out=- (-3.19), phase=2 (-2.62), orig6=- (-2.33), in_first=0 (-1.79).
